_comment: Tombstone registry for deliberately-removed events. When an owner deletes a row from public/data/events.json that Ticketmaster still lists (e.g. a de-duplicated or dead-storefront copy), add it here so the 04:00 new-show recogniser (scripts/sync-ticketmaster-events.py) does not re-propose it. Entries only ever WITHHOLD a re-discovered show — they can never publish one. See docs/PROVIDER_SYNC.md. Match is by either Ticketmaster id OR venue/date, mirroring the live dedup keys.

_schema.artist_slug: required — the artist the deleted event belonged to
_schema.id: recommended — the deleted row's events.json id, the event's permanent TTC identity (its price history, /api/out showId and future event URL key all derive from it); not used for matching
_schema.ticketmaster_discovery_event_id: optional — Discovery API id of the deleted row (matched case-insensitively)
_schema.ticketmaster_event_id: optional — storefront id / intl URL slug of the deleted row (matched case-insensitively)
_schema.venue: optional (with a date) — venue name of the deleted row
_schema.datetime_iso: optional — the deleted row's datetime_iso; used with timezone to derive the venue-local date for the venue/date key
_schema.timezone: optional — IANA timezone of the deleted row (improves venue-local date accuracy)
_schema.local_date: optional — YYYY-MM-DD venue-local date; overrides datetime_iso/timezone derivation when present
_schema.reason: recommended — human note on why the row was removed
_schema.deleted_at: recommended — ISO date the row was tombstoned
_schema.canonical_id: optional — for a removed duplicate, the retained row's events.json id (where its price history and provider identity continue); not used for matching
